title: Reference frame of left/right and front/behind
question: Session KO-R2 marked the four space construction rows (assertion/train, truth_question/dev_a, reported_clause/dev_b, conditional/test) with issue=yes: '왼쪽/오른쪽 and 앞/뒤 frame-ambiguous; state viewer perspective explicitly'. The other sessions' rows for the same constructions in all three languages are attached as data (EN 'to the left of'/'in front of', DE 'links von'/'vor', KO '왼쪽에'/'앞에' are the corresponding terms). Question: under the stated task definition, are the two sentences of a pair read in one common reference frame, so that the converse relation (A left of B <=> B right of A; A in front of B <=> B behind A) holds and the reference labels are determined? Is there an admissible interpretation under which a reference label changes? Apply exactly the same criterion to English, German and Korean, and state whether the vertical axis (above/below) differs. Give a concrete counterexample if one exists.
